previous_disclosures.summary: Complex large language models (LLMs) and large vision models (LVMs) are disrupting traditional search and content creation methods by offering enhancements in consumer utility. Qualcomm believes innovative enterprise and consumer use cases will emerge as these models run on-device, leveraging multiple sensor modalities to provide immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2024 disclosures cover the landscape of AI model investment (LLMs, SLMs, etc.), their disruption of user experiences, and the strategic view that these models must run on-device for privacy and utility. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) covers the exact same specific points: the development of LLMs/SLMs/LVMs/LMMs, their disruption of search/content, and the necessity of on-device execution for utility, privacy, and security. qcom_2024_1_D011 maps to the model landscape/disruption, and qcom_2024_1_D012 maps to the on-device necessity/utility argument found in qcom_2025_1_D010.

The 2024 disclosure expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities and increased adoption. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) contains the specific sentence: 'We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.' This is a direct textual and topical match.

previous_disclosures.summary: The market sees significant investment in LLMs, SLMs, LVMs, and LMMs for text, image, and multimodal applications, which are disrupting traditional search and content creation methods.
Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
Qualcomm expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities, with analysts estimating 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024.

current_disclosures.summary: Significant investment continues in developing various AI models (LLMs, SLMs, LVMs, LMMs) that disrupt traditional user experiences. While developed primarily for the cloud, these models must run on-device to maximize utility, privacy, and security, and the company expects continued advancement and adoption of generative AI capabilities in edge devices.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates discuss professional GPU hardware for rendering/CAD (D035) and client/gaming AI capabilities (D008), but do not address the specific strategic argument about generative AI utility requiring on-device execution or the privacy/security vs. cloud trade-off central to the target disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom address the tension between cloud-based generative AI development and the need for privacy/security, but they differ in execution strategy. Qualcomm advocates for on-device processing to maximize utility and privacy, whereas Broadcom offers a 'Private AI' solution that appears to focus on enabling generative AI usage within organizational boundaries (likely via VMware infrastructure) to satisfy compliance, without explicitly mandating on-device execution for consumers.

sentences.text: While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
• Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates focus on Intel's strategy to bring AI to the edge/AI PCs and their software/open-source initiatives (OpenVINO, oneAPI). While they mention 'edge' and 'AI PCs', they do not make the specific argument that generative AI *must* run on-device to maximize utility through privacy and immediacy in the manner Qualcomm does, nor do they contrast it with cloud development in the same specific value-proposition framework.

The retrieved candidates discuss memory bandwidth bottlenecks and storage solutions for AI data lakes. They do not address on-device generative AI execution strategies, privacy, or consumer utility arguments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Professional artists and designers use NVIDIA partner products for creative use cases, while generative AI expands the market for workstation-class GPUs as enterprises deploy AI applications on-premises.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify generative AI as a key driver for expanding the market for specific hardware classes, but they target different deployment environments. Qualcomm emphasizes the necessity of running AI on-device for consumer benefits like immediacy and privacy, while NVIDIA highlights enterprises developing and deploying AI applications on-premises, expanding the market for workstation-class GPUs.

sentences.text: While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
In addition, generative AI is expanding the market for our workstation-class GPUs, as more enterprise customers develop and deploy AI applications with their data on-premises.
